messages:
sam: quick thread — saw a perf regression on the speculative decoding canary this morning. latency p95 up ~28% when pairing qwen-14b drafts with mixtral-8x final. profiler attached below
ashley: ugh. is this the draft->final family mismatch we talked about?
mateo: can you paste the perf dump? curious if kernel selection flipped to the fallback path
sam: paste from perf script:
```
[profile summary]
model_pair: qwen-14b -> mixtral-8x
mean_lat: 210ms (baseline 165ms)
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.12 -> 0.34
batch_utilization: 0.62 -> 0.47
kernel_fallbacks: 87
spec_accept_rate: 0.41
roPE_scale_mismatch_warnings: 3
```
li: kv_cache_miss_rate jump is the biggest red flag. are tokenizers producing different canonicalized tokens so cache hits fail?
ashley: we saw tokenizer mismatch before when family mismatched (Qwen vs Mixtral) — even identical text can produce different subtokenization leading to low prefix hits
mateo: also check head/kv dims. mixtral-8x has kv_dim=128, qwen-14b uses 192 (example). runtime kernel chooser should detect mismatched kv layout and not try the cheap unified path
sam: kernel logs show we fell back to generic attention kernel for ~35% of steps because kernel selector failed to match the optimized kernel signatures
ops-bot: deploy-canaried: spec-decoder-v2 pushed to us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T08:12Z :white_check_mark:
ashley: that fallback path is much slower and doesn't use packed KV layout, hence the cache miss + latency. two things to consider: 1) prevent draft pairing across incompatible families, 2) make kernel selector tolerate head/kv dim permutations when safe
mateo: for (2) we can add a compatibility matrix: allow kernel reuse when (kv_dim ratio == 1 or quantization profile identical) and roPE scale close within 1e-3. otherwise force recompile.
li: roPE scaling — if qwen uses scale 1.0 and mixtral uses 0.97, the token positions drift and the draft acceptance drops, causing extra spec rounds and more KV churn. we saw spec_accept_rate at 0.41 which matches this behavior
sam: suggested short-term mitigations: 
- cap speculative drafts to same model family label (e.g., qwen.* -> qwen.* only)
- add a token-level fast-check: compare first 32 encoded ids between draft and final model tokenizers; if mismatch rate > 5% abort speculative decode
- force kernel selector to prefer optimized kv kernel only when kv_dim and dtype match exactly
ashley: also add metric around "speculative wasted tokens" (tokens generated by drafts that were discarded). that'll show cost impact clearly
mateo: profiling followups I can do today: dump full kernel selector decision trace with reasons, and produce a head/kv dimension histogram across models used in canaries.
li: small note — when we force family-only pairing we lose some latency wins (sometimes qwen draft + mixtral final is faster because of tokenization differences). need an acceptance tuning knob: target spec_accept_rate >= 0.6 and plan auto-rollbacks if below
sam: agreed. we should also expose a per-route override to allow mixed-family speculative pairing for opt-in routes where accuracy/latency tradeoffs are known
ops-bot: incident-tracker: ticket RI-4891 opened for speculative pairing perf regression by sam
ashley: I'll file a short RFC for kernel-selector changes. Mateo, can you own the perf trace and a quick canary to validate the token-level mismatch heuristic?
mateo: yep will run canary with token-prefix-check + family-lock and share results by EOD
sam: thanks. if we see little improvement, next step is to roll back speculative decoding on high-q routes until kernel selector patch lands :thumbsup:
